standard_prerequisites.name: Localization and limits
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the coequalizer of the zero map and Q(f) is represented by Q applied to the coequalizer of the zero map and f, which is what produces cokernels and their compatibility with the localization functor.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fraction representations in a left localization
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Categories, the description of a morphism of the localization as s^{-1} f with a common denominator
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the representation used at the start of the proof to reduce statements about an arbitrary morphism of the localization to statements about an image of a morphism of the original category.

standard_prerequisites.name: Abelian categories through coimage and image
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of an abelian category by the coincidence of coimage and image
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the remaining axiom that part (3) has to verify.

core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 2144-2152): for a morphism a of the localization written as s^{-1} f, the image Q(s) is an isomorphism, so the existence of the cokernel of a is equivalent to that of the cokernel of Q(f), and the latter is Q of the cokernel of f by the cited lemma on limits in localizations.
Part (2) (proof line 2155): the statement about kernels in a right localization is dual to part (1).

Part (3) (proof lines 2157-2164): if S is a multiplicative system then it is both a left and a right multiplicative system, so the localization has kernels and cokernels and the functor commutes with them; finally every arrow of the localization is isomorphic to the image of an arrow of the original category, which reduces the verification that coimage and image coincide to the corresponding fact in the abelian category.
proof_roadmap: Reduce a morphism of the localization to one in the image of the functor and identify its cokernel.
Combine the two to get an abelian category and reduce the last axiom to the original category.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that localizing an abelian category at a left multiplicative system produces cokernels commuting with the localization functor, at a right multiplicative system produces kernels, and at a multiplicative system produces an abelian category with the localization functor exact (statement lines 2127-2141). The proof is a complete argument: part (1) reduces an arbitrary morphism of the localization to the image of a morphism of the original category and identifies its cokernel through the cited lemma on limits (proof lines 2144-2152); part (2) is dual; and part (3) combines the two and reduces the coincidence of coimage and image to the original category (proof lines 2157-2164). The non-formal content is the reduction to a morphism in the image of the functor. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
